lesson.text: Quick memory: what is a win-win deal? (Good for both people.) Today: pitching an idea, taking feedback and saying no to unfair deals.
A strong pitch has four parts: the PROBLEM, your IDEA, WHY YOU, and WHAT YOU NEED (and what they get back).
Look at your listeners, stand tall and speak clearly. Facts they can check build trust.
A hard question? Answer honestly. 'I'll find out' is better than making something up.
Feedback is free advice: say thank you, ask a question, then decide.
Not every deal is a good deal. 'Sign now or it's gone!' is a pressure trick: take your time, and ask a grown-up.
Try it in the practice room: pitch your bread cart to three investors.

exercises.prompt: It's OK to say 'I'll find out' when you don't know an answer.

exercises.explain: Problem, idea, why you, what you need.

exercises.prompt: 'Sign now or it's gone for ever!' is...
choices: a pressure trick: take your time
exercises.explain: It's a pressure trick: take your time.

exercises.prompt: You make 2 coins on each loaf. How many loaves pay back 50 coins?
You can say no politely to an unfair deal.

exercises.explain: Checkable facts and honest answers build trust.

exercises.prompt: Good feedback for a friend's pitch:
choices: 'I liked your sign. Next, say what you need.'
exercises.hint: One thing liked, one to try.
exercises.explain: One thing you liked and one thing to try.

exercises.prompt: An investor gets 1 coin of every 10 your cart makes. The cart makes 200 coins. How many go to the investor?
